notes: The Viva Viagem 24-hour pass costs 7 EUR (covers metro, trams and lifts; Sintra/Cascais trains are not included and cost 2.45 separately). The metro goes to the airport. The hills are steep; Bolt is cheap.
Summers are 28-32°C. The Santo António festival is in June (sardines in Alfama), Sintra is misty and cool, and the Cascais beaches are busy; August is crowded.
Pastel de nata 1.40, bica 1, bifana 4, restaurant meals 15-25. Send back the cover charge (bread/olives) if you don't want it. Round up the tip.
A timed ticket for Pena in Sintra is REQUIRED (online, 09:30 in the morning); book Jerónimos online too. Most museums are closed on Mondays.
There are pickpockets on tram 28. At night in Bairro Alto, people offering to sell you drugs are fake; ignore them.
Bacalhau (salt cod) comes in 365 recipes, sardines are in season June-August, and ginjinha (sour cherry liqueur) costs 1.50 EUR at Rossio.

transit.name: Viva Viagem / Navegante
transit.why_chosen: 24 hours for 7 EUR on the metro, trams, buses, lifts and the Sintra/Cascais trains

stops.name: Miradouro de Santa Luzia
stops.tips: Azulejo-tiled terrace with views over the Tejo and the Alfama rooftops in the morning light.

stops.name: Castelo de São Jorge
stops.tips: Moorish castle with peacocks and 360° city views. Buy tickets online to skip the queue, then walk down through the streets of Alfama.

stops.name: Tasca do Chico Alfama
stops.tips: Sardines and bifana (pork sandwich), with fado in the evening (no reservations, 20:00).

stops.name: Tram 28 Martim Moniz
stops.tips: The yellow tram runs from Graça to Estrela. Use a 24-hour pass, watch for pickpockets and board at Martim Moniz.

stops.name: Miradouro da Graça
stops.tips: Views of the castle and the bridge, with a kiosk beer at sunset.

backups.name: A Baiuca Alfama
backups.tips: Amateur fado (vadio) tavern; set menu required.

backups.name: Panteão Nacional
backups.tips: White-domed pantheon with a terrace. An alternative to Alfama; Tuesday is the Feira da Ladra flea market.

stops.name: Mosteiro dos Jerónimos
stops.tips: Manueline masterpiece of a monastery with Vasco da Gama's tomb. Book a timed ticket online (the queue is 1 hour); closed on Mondays.

stops.name: Pastéis de Belém
stops.tips: Bakery dating from 1837. Have a warm pastel de nata with cinnamon; the tiled rooms inside have no queue.

stops.name: Torre de Belém
stops.tips: UNESCO riverside fortress, with the Monument to the Discoveries on the way. The outside is enough (the queue to go in is 1 hour).

stops.name: MAAT Museum
stops.tips: Wave-shaped museum on the riverbank. Walk on the roof; LX Factory is across the way.

stops.name: LX Factory
stops.tips: Factory complex with the Ler Devagar bookshop and design shops; there is a market on Sundays.

backups.name: Museu Nacional dos Coches
backups.tips: Royal carriages; an alternative to MAAT.

stops.name: Palácio da Pena
stops.tips: Train from Rossio, 40 minutes (2.45 EUR), then bus 434. Colourful romantic palace; an online timed ticket is REQUIRED, first slot 09:30. The terrace is free and may be misty.

stops.name: Castelo dos Mouros
stops.tips: Moorish walls with views of Pena, a 10-minute walk away.

stops.name: Sintra Tarihi Merkez
stops.tips: Try travesseiro (puff pastry pillow) and queijada (small cheese tart) at Piriquita; the town square is nearby.

stops.name: Quinta da Regaleira
stops.tips: Masonic garden with the spiral Initiation Well and tunnels; quiet at the end of the day.

stops.name: Sintra Tren Istasyonu Dönüş
stops.tips: Train back to Rossio, or bus 403 to Cabo da Roca (for summer sunsets).

backups.name: Palácio Nacional de Sintra
backups.tips: Royal palace with twin chimneys, in town; an alternative to Regaleira.

stops.name: Praça do Comércio
stops.tips: Square opening onto the river; terrace on the Rua Augusta Arch (4 EUR).

stops.name: Convento do Carmo
stops.tips: Gothic church whose roof collapsed in the 1755 earthquake; the nave is open to the sky.

stops.name: A Brasileira Chiado
stops.tips: Pessoa's café: have a bica (espresso) and take a photo with his statue.

stops.name: Time Out Market Lisboa
stops.tips: Chef stalls at Cais do Sodré; try the Manteigaria pastel de nata.

stops.name: Bairro Alto & Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara
stops.tips: A bohemian neighbourhood for the evening, with terrace views and the Pink Street bars.

backups.name: Cervejaria Ramiro
backups.tips: Legendary seafood beer hall; finish with prawns and a bifana. Expect a queue.

backups.name: Museu Nacional de Arte Antiga
backups.tips: Bosch's Temptation of Saint Anthony; an alternative to Time Out.

stops.name: Cascais Praia da Rainha
stops.tips: Train from Cais do Sodré, 40 minutes. Beach and marina of a fishing town.

stops.name: Boca do Inferno
stops.tips: The Hell's Mouth cliffs, with crashing waves.

stops.name: Marisco na Praça Cascais
stops.tips: Seafood inside the market, sold by weight.

stops.name: Cabo da Roca
stops.tips: The westernmost point of Europe. Bus 403 takes 30 minutes; lighthouse, cliffs and wind.

stops.name: Praia do Guincho
stops.tips: Surf beach with dunes; return to Cascais afterwards.

backups.name: Estoril Casino & Tamariz
backups.tips: Estoril beach and Europe's largest casino; an alternative to Cabo.

stops.name: Museu Nacional do Azulejo
stops.tips: Tile museum with a 1738 panorama of Lisbon and a convent church.

stops.name: Oceanário de Lisboa
stops.tips: One of Europe's largest aquariums, on the Expo 98 site.

stops.name: Parque das Nações Nehir Kıyısı
stops.tips: Vasco da Gama Bridge (17 km) and the cable car.

stops.name: Vasco da Gama Alışveriş Merkezi Yemek Katı
stops.tips: A quick lunch with river views.

stops.name: Mouraria & Martim Moniz
stops.tips: The immigrant neighbourhood where fado was born: Severa's house and street art.

backups.name: Zé da Mouraria
backups.tips: Huge portions of bacalhau (salt cod) in Mouraria; lunch.

backups.name: Museu Calouste Gulbenkian
backups.tips: Lalique and Eastern art, plus a garden; an alternative to the aquarium.

stops.name: Cais do Sodré Feribot Cacilhas
stops.tips: A 10-minute ferry to the other side of the Tejo.

stops.name: Cristo Rei
stops.tips: Sibling of Rio's Christ. Take the lift up 80 m for a panorama of Lisbon; bus 101.

stops.name: Ponto Final Cacilhas
stops.tips: Yellow tables on the riverbank. A farewell lunch with views of Lisbon; book ahead.

stops.name: Aeroporto Metro
stops.tips: Red line metro, 25 minutes. Farewell.

backups.name: Mercado da Ribeira Sabahı
backups.tips: Market at Cais do Sodré; an alternative to Cristo Rei.
